# Dentist Niche

Dentist guidance applies to dental-practice, orthodontic, oral-surgery, and similar healthcare-practice websites. It is not general premium-web guidance. A dentist site needs calm, medical trust, and human warmth; other niches may need different typography, color, imagery, density, and motion rules.

Read the universal rules first:

- [Design](../../Design/linker_Design.md): token usage, interaction semantics, link patterns, motion, radius.
- [Styles](../../Styles/linker_Styles.md): token mechanics and Tailwind-vs-CSS implementation.
- [Fonts](../../Fonts/linker_Fonts.md): font configuration, preloading, self-hosting, and debugging.

Then apply only the dentist-specific leaves that fit the project:

- [Register](register.md): dentist-specific visual register, restrained color direction, imagery boundaries, and interaction tone.
- [Typography](typography.md): when a premium dentist site can use serif display type plus sans functional UI, and where that rule stops.
- [Tiers](Tiers/linker_Tiers.md): routing notes for dentist preview tiers such as Partner / Tier 3. This composes general Design rules with dentist register and project Brand docs.

## Boundaries

- Do not copy dentist typography rules into SaaS, agency, restaurant, portfolio, legal, or product sites without a fresh design argument.
- Do not store exact brand colors here. A dental practice may choose botanical, clinical, warm-neutral, mineral, blue, or another restrained direction depending on the client brand.
- Do not store exact font-family picks here. Font family choices belong in the project font config and brand docs.
- Do not store feature matrices, pricing, page counts, or package promises here. Commercial tier details belong in project docs.
- Do not add code examples here unless they are intentionally copyable templates. Put copyable artifacts in `Templates/` and link to them.
